clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's return, 1989–1994
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Gordon coming back into the family in early 1989, within five years: your move to Quarry Lane that spring, late nights through secondary school from autumn 1989, settling into the rebuilt Hollin Road house that fall, your mother filling in your college forms in 1991, your grandfather's death in June 1991, your move to the conservatory that September where you leaned hard on Rafe, a wrist injury that stopped your playing in October, a blow-up with Rafe in November, getting high and absorbed in fixing radios through the winter, feeling lost and low with your grandfather gone and your mother about to remarry, earning money fixing radios in spring 1992, your stepparents' wedding that October, and by January 1994 you were stung that your dad had never heard of the film you were making and you found your drive again in Portugal. The shifts pile up from your move into the rebuilt house alongside your late nights and your mother taking over your choices, then cluster thick around your grandfather's death and your time at the conservatory; the quiet that follows your return to coursework and your exchanges abroad marks where things settled.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death, 2008–2009
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Lorna dying in January 2008, within a year: four weeks building with Silas at Alder Creek in July 2008 where you were too drained for conversation with your mother, she pressed to visit you and you kept the door shut on her, and you left for nursing school and stopped speaking to your mother when you moved to Marlow Sound that August. Your mother's push to visit and your conflict with her sit close in time at the lodge, then you cut off all contact as you left for school; the silence held for roughly a year.

clusters.name: Your marriage to Wren, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Around your marriage to Wren in March 2017, within roughly two years: you saw your mother a bit less once Wren came along, your cousin Alice diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in October 2017, your sister flying for a regional airline and married by summer 2018, a family holiday that summer where you and Imogen barely talked, your aunt Imogen lashing out when muddled, your mother had a heart check-up and all was clear, your job steadied and paid well by June 2019, your partner's brother Leo returned to Danfield with his family, you felt constantly that you ought to be driving projects forward and started a sleeping pill in October 2019, you aimed for shorter regular calls with your mother, your sister expecting her first baby, Wren swamped by a street party, a fundraising dinner and a drive to the lake for her mother's retirement, you laid out a plan too strict to settle her, Wren talks with her father and brother all day with nothing happening to one that the others don't hear, she settled once the weekend had a plan, you awoke from the small hours at the lake weekend with no more sleep and could only pull back, and you felt anxious when you'd had no sleep at family occasions. The shifts gather around Wren's arrival and her family's life—her mother's retirement party and her brother's return—drawing your anxiety up and your distance into her family's closeness.

periods.name: the year I left home
periods.words: The first is the year I left home: I went off to the conservatory, hurt my wrist in the first term and couldn't play, dropped out and drifted at my mother's place, then spent a bleak spell at the community college shooting pool every night until an exchange in Portugal snapped me out of it and I tore through the rest of my coursework.

periods.name: the long slump
periods.words: The second is the long slump, roughly ages 27 to 29, when nothing at home felt right, I moved to Gull Harbour away from nearly everyone I knew, then followed Marisol to Fenwick, and when that fell apart I went under, a depression I only really climbed out of after nursing school.
